name: Qin Jiushao’s congruence algorithm
description: Qin Jiushao described a systematic method for solving simultaneous integer congruences.

date.basis: Year of the dated publication, or a broad historian-estimated composition interval; no first discovery claimed.

events.statement: Qin Jiushao’s Mathematical Work in Nine Chapters described congruence methods in 1247.

evidence.supports: Dates the mathematical book to 1247 and describes congruence algorithms.
Explains its method of solving simultaneous integer congruences.
Dates the mathematical book to 1247 and describes congruence algorithms.

earliest_record.rationale: Dated witness within the inspected evidence; not a global-priority claim.

caveats: The 1247 text is a dated presentation, not the origin of Chinese remainder problems or a claim of worldwide priority; earlier Chinese mathematical traditions contributed. Qin said he learned the rule from calendar specialists at the Board of Astronomy; the exact contributions of those specialists are not otherwise resolved here.

research.note: Independent reading checked the source-supported event and chronology. Grain and other unreviewed facets remain provisional.

links.statement: Qin’s 1247 treatise was modeled in part on the earlier Nine Chapters handbook; this concerns the work’s structure and does not establish the origin of its congruence algorithm.

evidence.supports: Describes Qin’s treatise as modeled to some extent on the Nine Chapters.
